root_cause: The original Composio v3.1 session-create request used toolkits.enabled, taken from a normalized RESPONSE field. The official session CREATE request and SDK require toolkits.enable. The 400 TOOLKIT_CONSTRAINT is consistent with this mistake, although causal resolution still requires an authenticated live retry. The earlier legacy direct-execution fallback returned successful:false, but does not prove the API key lacks permissions. The owner displayed two Full access project API keys; no underlying Vault secret value was inspected.
prevention: Use documented create-request wire contract {toolkits:{enable:['netlify_mcp']}}. Never derive request parameters from normalized response examples. Require static regression rejecting 'toolkits.enabled', preserve one OIDC-authorized user/account/site and read-only health vs deploy separation. Keep strict existing GitHub checks and provider readback, no synthetic green.
